partial_case.facts: The resident has been the leaseholder of the property since November 2023; the property is a 3-bedroom ground and first floor maisonette. Before the resident became leaseholder, the previous owner made multiple reports of a leak from the flat above between February 2022 and November 2023. From November 2023 the resident reported that the leak occurred whenever it rained, and from February to July 2024 the landlord carried out repairs that did not resolve the leak. On 23 September 2024 the resident complained that she had been reporting an ongoing leak in one bedroom since November 2023, that repairs had not resolved it, and that the property was cold, damp and mouldy. The resident asked for a lasting repair and requested her housing file, job records, the roof survey report, and a timeline and proposed works for fixing the roof. The landlord issued a stage 1 response on 27 September 2024 and a stage 2 response on 19 December 2024. On 25 February 2025 the resident asked the Service to investigate, saying the leak was ongoing, the property was damp and cold, and the issues had affected her health and finances because she could not rent out the room.
